title: How to Justify a 2x-3x Salary Hike to HR
summary: The creator discusses how to handle the common issue where HR questions a large salary hike, such as going from 6 LPA to 12-15 LPA. The main lesson is to avoid letting your current CTC become the benchmark and instead justify your worth based on the value you bring.
key_points: Do not let your current CTC become the benchmark for your next salary.
Make HR understand why you are worth the compensation you are asking for.
Do not justify a high hike by saying you worked really hard.
Do not justify a high hike by saying your current company doesn't pay well.
Do not justify a high hike by saying you have X years of experience.
Do not justify a high hike by saying you have a lot of responsibilities.
Do not justify a high hike by saying you need at least a certain amount like 12 LPA.
content:
Post: Here’s how you can justify the big salary jump in the interviews. Even if they don’t ask you this question directly, you should already have a strong answer ready. Because if you don’t have a confident answer to “Why should we pay you this much?” Your negotiation is already over. Strong candidates don’t negotiate based on what they used to earn. They negotiate based on the value they can bring. Your last salary is your history. It should not decide your future. Make a note of this post.

The 2X-3X Salary Hike Guide How to justify a much higher salary to HR or a recruiter without sounding entitled, desperate, or unrealistic 1. First, understand the real problem Let's say: Your current CTC = ₹6 LPA You get shortlisted for a role paying up to ₹12-15 LPA. You perform very well in the interviews HR then says: "We really liked your profile, but your current CTC is ₹6 LPA. A 2X hike is difficult for us to justify." Most candidates immediately start defending their old salary. They say: "But I've worked really hard." "My current company doesn't pay well." "I have 4 years of experience." "I have a lot of responsibilities." "My friends are earning more." "I need at least ₹12 LPA." That's usually the wrong direction. Your job isn't to prove that ₹6 LPA is a bad salary. Your job is to explain: Why the compensation you're asking for makes sense for the new role and for the value you can bring. That is the fundamental shift. 2.
